answer: Seats can be bound to tokens software cannot copy. Each agent holds a small ferrous slug with a hollow chamber, sealed by a violet dye pellet and random grain. A bench reader reads eddy-current phase and chamber resonance, a fingerprint that drifts with wear, so it is re-checked every epoch. Registration matches the pellet spectral line to the chamber mode; one channel alone fails. Running N identities needs N slugs, N readers, and N real hands for the thermal warm-up, since readers need a live ramp. A cheap key becomes hardware and labor cost scaling linearly, which no sybil budget absorbs.
